info.title: Promotional site with rich markdown docs for Pathland

parts.text: I want to build a website using pathland that promotes it and also delivers a documentaion for it. For the documentation sites I would prefer to to be able to describe it using markdown. Not markdown via text views, as we need support for more markdown (images, table etc.). What do you think we lack to be able to build such a website?

The user wants to build a website using Pathland that promotes it and delivers documentation. They want documentation described in Markdown with support for full markdown (images, tables, etc.), not just the inline markdown currently supported via text views. They ask: "What do you think we lack to be able to build such a website?"

I need to research the codebase to understand current capabilities and gaps. Let me explore.

Key areas:
- Markdown support: `pathland-markdown` (no_std inline parser into AttributedString) — only inline (bold/italic/code/strike/links), no blocks, tables, images, headings, lists.
- HTML renderer capabilities: which primitives are implemented (VSTACK, HSTACK, TEXT, IMAGE, etc.)
- Whether there's a block-level markdown renderer (likely not).
- Whether there's SSR static site generation, routing, etc.
- Documentation components needed: code blocks with syntax highlighting, tables, headings with anchors/TOC, images, callouts, navigation/sidebar, search.
- Also the promotion site: layout, images, video, etc.

Let me look through the repo to determine what exists and what's missing. I should use explore agents and direct reads.

Let me first check the specs and renderer statuses. Let me run some searches.

state.output: # pathland-markdown — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 The **shared inline Markdown parser**: `no_std` + `alloc`, used by the Rust DSL directly and by foreign hosts through `pathland-markdown-capi`. It produces a `pathland_core::AttributedString` (style runs + links), not a separate AST. ## Implemented - Inline subset: `**bold**` / `__bold__` → `FONT_WEIGHT` 700, `*italic*` / `_italic_` → `FONT_STYLE` Italic, `` `code` `` → `FONT_DESIGN` Monospaced, `~~strikethrough~~` → `STRIKETHROUGH`, `[label](url)` → link run (label parsed recursively), and backslash escapes. - Nested emphasis with run splitting (`***`/`___` close italic then bold); intraword underscores stay literal (`snake_case`). - UTF-8 byte offsets in the produced runs; code spans do not parse inner markup. - Unit tests for markers, nesting, links, code, escapes, underscores, unmatched markers, and UTF-8 offsets. - Used by the Rust DSL: `pathland-engine` auto-parses `Node::markdown_text`. The Kotlin `Text(...)` path uses a **pure-Java behavioural port** in `pathland-view-core` (no native library); `pathland-markdown-capi` remains for non-JVM hosts. ## Not implemented / gaps - Block Markdown (headings, lists, paragraphs), reference links, images, and tables. --- # pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming** pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once, and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`. > **JVM note:** the Spring Boot / Quarkus paths no longer load this crate through > JNA. `lib/java/pathland-render-html` is a **pure-Java behavioural port**, and > `GoldenConformanceTest` keeps it byte-identical to this canonical renderer. > The Rust crate remains the cross-language (C ABI) implementation and the > source of the committed golden fixtures. ## Implemented - **Window metadata → head**: `TITLE` → ``, `DESCRIPTION` → `<meta name="description">`, `LOCALE` → `<html lang>` (default `en`/`Pathland`); values escaped. Also: generic `LABEL` → `aria-label` (icon buttons), slider names on the inner input, `aria-hidden` on the non-visual media shell. - **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta` is a per-render host option (`render_document_with_meta` / `render_document_linked_with_meta`) for the canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter cards, and JSON-LD. Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` still win; `DocumentMeta` title/description are fallbacks. JSON-LD derives a `WebPage` plus one `Article` per `ROLE_ARTICLE` (headline from the first heading, description from the first paragraph, image from the first `IMAGE`); `<`/`>`/`&` are unicode-escaped so app text cannot break out of the script element. `pathland_html_render_with_meta` exposes the same option over the C ABI (`PathlandHtmlMeta`). The canonical Rust output is pinned by `document_meta.document.html` and the Java port reproduces it byte-for-byte. - **`PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E)**: renders as a plain container box (a flex column, like a stack with one child) and lays out the (id-remapped) origin subtree the proxying server spliced in — the renderer holds no notion of "remote" (spec/PROXY.md §5). Without this arm the component fell to the `_ => String::new()` default and the spliced subtree was dropped. Covered by a unit test. - **Attributed text**: `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` decodes the binary payload into the node model and renders non-overlapping `<span style>` runs plus `<a href>` links (v1 attributes: font size/weight/color/style/design/underline/ strikethrough); text and URLs are escaped, and the plain text remains the fallback. Covered by a unit test. - **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)` / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML; the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed. - **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy: `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER` (inline `flex:1`), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` (`data-min`/`data-max` ride on the gauge so the DOM client can recompute its percentage), `VSTACK`/ `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/ `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD` (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE` (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER` (the `.pathland-stepper` composite with `data-min`/`data-max`/`data-step` on its hidden range span), `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` → `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children rendered as `<option data-pathland-id="{child}" value="{index}">` + `SELECTION`), `MENU` (the `.pathland-menu` composite: `.pathland-menu-trigger` label + `.pathland-menu-items` children), `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`. - **Native elements** (the specs carry no renderer mappings — this is the concrete HTML map the removed spec hints lived in): `TEXT` → `<span>` (or `<p>`/`<h1>`–`<h5>` by `ROLE`/heading `TEXT_STYLE`), `IMAGE` → `<img>`, `ICON` → inline **Remix (filled)** `<svg class="pathland-icon">` (the canonical `ICON_NAME` resolves to its filled SVG markup via this renderer's own `icons` module (`crate::icons`, the web owner of the mapping); the svg carries `data-pathland-icon="<name>"` — the DOM client's lazy resolver reads it as an embedded glyph for instant on-page swaps; `LABEL` → `role="img"` + `aria-label`, none → `aria-hidden`; sized `1em` so `FONT_SIZE` scales it, tinted via `fill="currentColor"`), `SIZE_THAT_FITS` → `<div class="pathland-ftf">` (the fit slot: fill-sized with `data-pathland-fit` mirroring the `FIT_QUERY` LIST, decoded as `[count][f32×count]` at decode time — the DOM client derives the fit locally and reports `FIT_CHANGED` on transitions; the slot is layout-transparent, forwarding the parent flex container's `flex-direction`/`align-items`/`justify-content` (`inherit`) into its own box so a wrapper never pins a centered candidate to the start — `VStack(CENTER)` > fit slot > `HSTACK` keeps centering; stays size-taking via `flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;min-width/height:0`), and the **web-SSR snapshot form** (issue #141: the slot carries EVERY candidate, in `FIT_QUERY` order — the protocol's candidate-identity contract) renders each branch in a `data-pathland-fit-cand="i" data-pathland-fit-cand-id="<child>"` gate wrapper whose inline `display` is the pre-CSS default (candidate 0 `contents`, every other candidate `none`), marks the slot as the query context (`container-type:inline-size; container-name:pf-<id>`), and emits the `@container` **band rules** into a `<style data-pathland-fit>` head element: for each distinct threshold `T_i` (`i ≥ 1`, ascending) a self-contained `@container pf-<id> (min-width: T_i)` band that **hides every candidate `j ≠ i` and shows candidate `i`**, so the highest matching band wins and **exactly one** candidate is visible at any width (no band for `T_0`; below the first band the inline default shows candidate 0). A no-JS first paint therefore already shows the candidate matching the slot's width; the single-child live form is unchanged. The bands are **SSR-only** — the first `FIT_CHANGED` collapses the slot to the live single-child form and the DOM client removes the gating (`collapseFitSlotFor` unwraps the gate wrappers, strips the container/candidate attrs, and `dropFitBandRules` deletes the slot's rules)), `COLOR` → `<div>`, `SHAPE` → CSS shapes / inline SVG, `DIVIDER` → `<hr>`, `SPACER` → inline flex filler, `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `<progress>` / `.pathland-spinner`, `GAUGE` → `.pathland-gauge`, stacks/lazy stacks → flex `div`, `ZSTACK` → grid overlay `div`, grids → CSS-grid `div`, `SCROLLVIEW` → overflow `div` (**gap: `SCROLL_AXIS` 0x0021 not yet implemented** — still both-axis greedy), `BUTTON` → `<button>`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `<input>` (secure → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR` → `<textarea>`, `TOGGLE` → checkbox/switch input, `SLIDER` → `<input type="range">`, `STEPPER` → `.pathland-stepper`, `DATE_PICKER` → `<input type="date">`/`<input type="time">`, `PICKER` → `<select>` + `<option>`, `MENU` → `.pathland-menu` composite, `COLOR_PICKER` → `<input type="color">`, `VIDEO` → `<video controls>`, `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` → an off-flow (`position:absolute;1px;opacity:0`) shell (non-visual, layout-transparent — **not** `display:none`, which silences the `<video>`'s audio), `COMMENT` → none. - **Media (spec/MEDIA.md)**: `IMAGE` renders `<img src alt>` (the `LABEL` accessibility text is the `alt`; empty = decorative) and honors `CONTENT_MODE`/`ASPECT_RATIO` inline (`Fit`→`object-fit:contain`, `Fill`→`object-fit:cover`); a `VIDEO` surface renders `<video data-pathland-controller="C" controls>` (the binding attribute appears only when the surface references a controller). **Audio has no view.** A **`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`** is non-visual and layout-transparent: it renders an off-flow shell carrying the resource (`data-pathland-media-controller` + `data-pathland-media-src`), which the DOM client turns into the playback (keyed by the controller id; spec/EVENTS.md Media). Asset refs are absolute (`/_pathland/assets/…`); bytes never ride the opcode stream. - **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render the custom body wrapped in the native element. - **Native browser controls inherit the design system**: the Tailwind-derived preflight stays the base reset, and every native form control carries a `pathland-*` class styled from design tokens: - text fields/editors: `.pathland-input.pathland-control`; - `PICKER` → `.pathland-select.pathland-control` (native dropdown arrow kept, tokenized field + options); - `DATE_PICKER` / `COLOR_PICKER` → `.pathland-date` / `.pathland-color` with `.pathland-control` (tokenized surface, inherited `color-scheme`, `accent-color`); - `SLIDER` → `.pathland-slider` with a renderer-owned track/thumb (`slider.track` / `slider.accent` / `slider.thumb`), no native range chrome; the `--pl-slider-fill` custom property is emitted inline for first paint and kept in sync by the DOM client (value/min/max/input). The native range input remains for keyboard/pointer interaction and accessibility; - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `.pathland-progress` with tokenized WebKit/Mozilla track/fill pseudo-elements; - `VIDEO` → `.pathland-video` (and `.pathland-media` for custom bodies) with surface/radius/accent tokens. Inline opcode properties still override the base classes. Native `<select>` popups, date/color dialogs, and `<video>` controls remain UA shadow DOM, so their internals are best-effort; app-driven media is fully themeable. - **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis **position** — the default is hug (`flex-start`), never CSS `align-items:stretch`, per `spec/LAYOUT.md`; only `FILL`-sized children stretch via their `100%` size), `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL` → `width:100%`/`height:100%` expansion, `HUG` → intrinsic), the frame bounds `MIN_WIDTH`/`IDEAL_WIDTH`/`MAX_WIDTH` and the height equivalents (emitted on the SSR first paint, matching the DOM client), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `TEXT_STYLE` (the renderer-owned default size/weight; explicit `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT` override), `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`, `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT` (positive → `-webkit-box`/`-webkit-line-clamp` **with `overflow:hidden`** — the clamp draws the ellipsis but does not clip on its own, so Safari would otherwise paint the overflowed text below the box, matching the DOM client), `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`, `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA), plus `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `COLOR_INVERT`. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `HUG_CONTENT` (-2) is **omitted** (intrinsic size); `FILL` (-1) → `100%`. - **`SHADOW_*` (box-shadow)**: a non-zero `SHADOW_RADIUS` (or an `SHADOW_X`/`SHADOW_Y` offset) emits `box-shadow: <color> <x>px <y>px <radius>px` (color first — the canonical order a browser serializes back to, so the SSR string matches the hydrated DOM). The color is `SHADOW_COLOR` when set, else the **renderer-owned default `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`** — so a `shadow(radius)` modifier (radius only; the color is renderer-owned) already draws before hydration, matching the DOM client. - **`Z_INDEX` (draw-order override)**: a `ZSTACK` child's `Z_INDEX` is emitted on its **shell** (the grid item that participates in stacking — the child's own `z-index` is inert inside the shell), so a higher value draws above lower siblings regardless of child index (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack). **Every shell carries an explicit `z-index`** (the child's `Z_INDEX`, else `0`) and the ZStack container sets `isolation:isolate`, so overlapping grid items paint deterministically in every browser (WebKit paints a non-fill grid item below a full-area sibling when both are `z-index:auto`). Mirrored by the DOM client's `applyLayout`. - **Layout contract (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: cross-axis default is **hug** (`flex-start`), not CSS stretch; `ALIGNMENT` positions only (`Fill`=3 → hug default). `DIVIDER` is greedy on the cross axis (`width:100%`); `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy on both axes (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch`); fixed frames emit exact px boxes. Conformance cases C1–C6 asserted in `lib.rs` tests. - **Fill propagation (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §stack layout model)**: implemented — `fills_axis` resolves a Hug stack/ZStack containing a `FILL` child / greedy primitive on an axis as `FILL`, emitting `width/height:100%` on that axis, and cross-axis `FILL` children stretch via `align-self:stretch` (SSR + TS DOM client, kept canonical via the layout pass in `applyLayout`). - **ZStack (spec/PRIMITIVES.md)**: implemented — an overlapping grid (`grid-area:1/1` cells); the container hugs to its largest child (`max-content`) unless Fixed/FILL (or fill propagation → `100%`); each child keeps its own size and is positioned by `ALIGNMENT` on both axes (SSR + TS DOM client). **Grid tracks are `minmax(0,1fr)`** (ZStack + count-generated grid tracks, `repeat(n,minmax(0,1fr))`, and lazy-hgrid auto columns), so a FILL ZStack/grid can shrink below its content min-height on a short viewport — an `end`-aligned child (e.g. a player bar) stays pinned instead of being pushed out of view and the inner `ScrollView` scrolls. A `GRID_TRACKS` per-track spec is emitted verbatim (app-authored). **Child shells carry no explicit `width/height`** — `justify-self/align-self:stretch` only applies when a grid item's size is `auto`, so pinning `max-content` silently degraded `stretch` to `start` and a FILL child's `100%` resolved circularly (content height), overflowing the viewport. With `auto` sizes a FILL child genuinely stretches to its (shrinkable) track and a Hug child keeps content size + alignment. - **ARIA ROLE/STATE maps match the DOM client**: the full `ROLE` set (button… menu, incl. `text`/`img`/`radio`/`spinbutton`/`tablist`/`list`/`grid`/ `region`/`menu`) and the `STATE` semantics (one true `aria-*` per state) are canonical with `lib/typescript/src/classes.ts`. - **Semantic HTML elements from `ROLE` + typography** (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties): a semantic role retags a **generic `div`/`span` shell** to its native element — `HEADER`→`<h2>`, `PARAGRAPH`→`<p>`, `LIST`→`<ul>`, `LIST_ITEM`→`<li>`, `SUMMARY`→`<section>`, and the landmarks `BANNER`→ `<header>`, `NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `MAIN`→`<main>`, `CONTENT_INFO`→`<footer>`, `COMPLEMENTARY`→`<aside>`, `ARTICLE`→`<article>`, `SECTION`→`<section>`, `SEARCH`→`<search>`. **Control components keep their native element** and emit no ARIA role from `ROLE` (`BUTTON` stays a `<button>`, `MENU` renders its intrinsic `role="menu"`). **Headings** come from a heading `TEXT_STYLE` typography (LargeTitle…Headline → `<h1>`–`<h5>`, always a heading) or from `ROLE_HEADER` (default `<h2>`); non-heading text defaults to `<span>`. Interactive/control roles are NOT in the catalog (intrinsic to the components); a custom button uses `Button`+`ButtonStyle`. The mapping lives in **`src/role_spec.rs`** (canonical with the DOM client — `pathland-ts-codegen` emits `generated/role-spec.ts`), with the role codes centralized in `pathland_core::constants::role`. - The color is `SHADOW_COLOR` when set, else the **renderer-owned default `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`** — so a `shadow(radius)` modifier (radius only; the color is renderer-owned) already draws before hydration, matching the DOM client. - **`Z_INDEX` (draw-order override)**: a `ZSTACK` child's `Z_INDEX` is emitted on its **shell** (the grid item that participates in stacking — the child's own `z-index` is inert inside the shell), so a higher value draws above lower siblings regardless of child index (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack). **Every shell carries an explicit `z-index`** (the child's `Z_INDEX`, else `0`) and the ZStack container sets `isolation:isolate`, so overlapping grid items paint deterministically in every browser (WebKit paints a non-fill grid item below a full-area sibling when both are `z-index:auto`). Mirrored by the DOM client's `applyLayout`. - **Layout contract (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: cross-axis default is **hug** (`flex-start`), not CSS stretch; `ALIGNMENT` positions only (`Fill`=3 → hug default). `DIVIDER` is greedy on the cross axis (`width:100%`); `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy on both axes (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch`); fixed frames emit exact px boxes. Conformance cases C1–C6 asserted in `lib.rs` tests. - **Fill propagation (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §stack layout model)**: implemented — `fills_axis` resolves a Hug stack/ZStack containing a `FILL` child / greedy primitive on an axis as `FILL`, emitting `width/height:100%` on that axis, and cross-axis `FILL` children stretch via `align-self:stretch` (SSR + TS DOM client, kept canonical via the layout pass in `applyLayout`). - **ZStack (spec/PRIMITIVES.md)**: implemented — an overlapping grid (`grid-area:1/1` cells); the container hugs to its largest child (`max-content`) unless Fixed/FILL (or fill propagation → `100%`); each child keeps its own size and is positioned by `ALIGNMENT` on both axes (SSR + TS DOM client). **Grid tracks are `minmax(0,1fr)`** (ZStack + count-generated grid tracks, `repeat(n,minmax(0,1fr))`, and lazy-hgrid auto columns), so a FILL ZStack/grid can shrink below its content min-height on a short viewport — an `end`-aligned child (e.g. a player bar) stays pinned instead of being pushed out of view and the inner `ScrollView` scrolls. A `GRID_TRACKS` per-track spec is emitted verbatim (app-authored). **Child shells carry no explicit `width/height`** — `justify-self/align-self:stretch` only applies when a grid item's size is `auto`, so pinning `max-content` silently degraded `stretch` to `start` and a FILL child's `100%` resolved circularly (content height), overflowing the viewport. With `auto` sizes a FILL child genuinely stretches to its (shrinkable) track and a Hug child keeps content size + alignment. - **ARIA ROLE/STATE maps match the DOM client**: the full `ROLE` set (button… menu, incl. `text`/`img`/`radio`/`spinbutton`/`tablist`/`list`/`grid`/ `region`/`menu`) and the `STATE` semantics (one true `aria-*` per state) are canonical with `lib/typescript/src/classes.ts`. - **Semantic HTML elements from `ROLE` + typography** (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties): a semantic role retags a **generic `div`/`span` shell** to its native element — `HEADER`→`<h2>`, `PARAGRAPH`→`<p>`, `LIST`→`<ul>`, `LIST_ITEM`→`<li>`, `SUMMARY`→`<section>`, and the landmarks `BANNER`→ `<header>`, `NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `MAIN`→`<main>`, `CONTENT_INFO`→`<footer>`, `COMPLEMENTARY`→`<aside>`, `ARTICLE`→`<article>`, `SECTION`→`<section>`, `SEARCH`→`<search>`. **Control components keep their native element** and emit no ARIA role from `ROLE` (`BUTTON` stays a `<button>`, `MENU` renders its intrinsic `role="menu"`). **Headings** come from a heading `TEXT_STYLE` typography (LargeTitle…Headline → `<h1>`–`<h5>`, always a heading) or from `ROLE_HEADER` (default `<h2>`); non-heading text defaults to `<span>`. Interactive/control roles are NOT in the catalog (intrinsic to the components); a custom button uses `Button`+`ButtonStyle`. The mapping lives in **`src/role_spec.rs`** (canonical with the DOM client — `pathland-ts-codegen` emits `generated/role-spec.ts`), with the role codes centralized in `pathland_core::constants::role`. - **`TREE::INSERT_CHILD` honors its `C` index** (`u32::MAX` = append), matching the protocol and the DOM client's `insertAt`. - **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` / `data-binding-id` attributes. - **Navigation slot attrs** (spec DSL.md §4.5 / MODIFIERS.md): a slot node's `ROUTE` (STRING) renders as `data-pathland-route="<path>"`, its `TRANSITION` hint renders as `data-pathland-transition="<platform|fade|slide|scale>"`, its `NAV_CHROME` (F32 enum) renders `data-pathland-nav-chrome="custom"` when `Custom` (the renderer adds no default chrome), and `NAV_DEPTH` (U32) renders `data-pathland-depth="N"` when deeper than its root so the DOM client can hydrate its default back button from the SSR HTML — the DOM renderer mirrors the route into the URL, may animate a swap, and draws the renderer's own back button (the web has no native navigation container). - `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time). - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md)**: - The naming/length conventions live in **`src/token_spec.rs`** — the single source of truth consumed by the renderer AND by `pathland-ts-codegen`, which emits the DOM client's `lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts` (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef`). - `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are collected per snapshot batch and emitted into the document head as CSS: base (light) tokens as `:root` rules, `dark.*` overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — the browser resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme. - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values resolve at render time to `var(--pl-…)`, with the generative `space.<N>` family resolving to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`Node::token_ref`). - **`STRING`-valued token overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`): a `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` with `valueType = STRING` resolves the value string from the batch's string section and emits it single-quoted (escaped) as a `:root` rule (or inside the dark media query). - The override rules render inside their own **`<style data-pathland-tokens>`** element in the document head, **after** the built-in block (so their `:root` variables win the cascade and the browser applies them) — matching the JS DOM client's `style[data-pathland-tokens]` element. No overrides → no extra element. - The built-in `:root` tokens use the **canonical spec paths** (`--pl-color-primary`, `--pl-color-background`, `--pl-color-text-primary`, `--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-border`) so app overrides retheme the renderer. - **Full Tier-1 default coverage**: `--pl-space-base` (light + dark, so the generative `space.<N>` family always resolves), canonical typography (`--pl-font-body-size/weight/family`), the radius scale + `--pl-border-width-thin`, the **shared control core** (`--pl-control-*`, `--pl-button-*`, `--pl-input-*`), and the component tokens (`--pl-toggle-*`, `--pl-slider-*`, `--pl-progress-*`, `--pl-gauge-*`, `--pl-stepper-*`, `--pl-picker-*`, `--pl-menu-*`, `--pl-label-*`, `--pl-size-control-*`), all with light + dark values. `.pathland-*` rules reference the canonical variables, so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides retheme components. - **Forced scheme**: `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` sets `data-pathland-scheme` on `<html>`; the platform-dark media rule is scoped to `:root:not([data-pathland-scheme])` and the dark values are repeated under `:root[data-pathland-scheme="dark"]`. Forced light suppresses the media rule. `META::RESET_THEME` clears the batch's overrides. - **Explicit `dark.` references** resolve to the forced-dark variable family (`--pl-dark-…`), so they use the dark value in either scheme. - **Unknown/unresolved token fallback**: `var(--pl-…, unset)` so the renderer's own default styling applies. Base overrides are repeated in the dark scope so they correctly outrank built-in dark defaults (dark override → base override → dark default). ## Built-in HTML base design (`design/`) The built-in stylesheet is now **generated**, not hand-written in `css.rs`: - `design/tokens/{base,semantic,component}` is a three-layer Style Dictionary source (flat DTCG entries). Base literals are compiled into literals and never emitted; semantic + component tokens are emitted in four layers (`:root`, platform-dark media, forced-dark/light scheme selectors, and the `--pl-dark-*` forced-dark family). - `design/html/{reset,components}.css` holds the hand-authored reset and `.pathland-*` rules. Component rules consume `var(--pl-*)` tokens; no design-relevant literal remains (sizes, radii, border widths, durations, z-index, focus rings, opacities). - `design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs` provide build/watch/validation. `check` verifies Tier-1 catalog coverage, layer/reference direction, dark/forced-dark declarations, `$extensions.pathland.internal` markings, and that every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by `token_spec::isLengthToken`. - `design/build/base.css` + `base.css.name` (the SHA-256 content hash, e.g. `base-5f86423db422.css`) are synced to `assets/` by `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` (and `--check` fails on drift). `src/css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!`; `builtin_css()` / `builtin_css_name()` expose them and `STYLE` wraps the bundle in `<style>`. - **External stylesheet mode**: `render_document` stays inline (the library default); `render_document_linked(opcodes, strings, root, css_base)` emits `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{css_base}/{name}">` instead. Token overrides and fit-band rules stay inline after it. The C ABI adds `pathland_html_render_linked`, `pathland_html_base_css`, and `pathland_html_base_css_name`; the Java port + Spring/Quarkus starters expose them and serve the CSS immutable. An empty base falls back to inline. - The design bundle is wired into the Maven `refresh-ide` profile and a CI design job that runs build/check/sync-check. ## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist: - **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`), including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment, text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds, hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**. - **`css::STYLE`** is the generated built-in `<style>` block injected by `render_document` (see "Built-in HTML base design" above), containing: - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`), - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-primary`, `--pl-color-background` (document background), `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-text-primary`/`--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-border`, `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, `--pl-input-*` (field bg/text/outline/ placeholder/focus), button tokens), named to match the canonical protocol design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme the renderer, - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme` dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/ disabled states that can't be expressed inline. Text fields use a Tailwind-style **inset outline** (`outline: 1px solid`, `outline-offset: -1px`, focus → `2px`/`-2px` + indigo) instead of a border, with dark-mode tokens; `html` sets `color-scheme: light dark` + the `--pl-color-bg` background so native form controls and the page follow the theme. - **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` / `_free`, plus `pathland_html_icon_svg`) for non-JVM cross-language hosts (Swift/.NET/…; the JVM uses the pure-Java port). `pathland_html_icon_svg(name)` returns the icon glyph's full `<svg>` (canonical name → glyph, unknown/extension → the renderer's fallback glyph) — how any host serves `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from ONE Rust source (the DOM client's lazy icon fetch) instead of per-platform static files. The `_tailwind_compile` entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`, `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**. Non-JVM hosts that embed the cdylib must refresh it with `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` (not just `cargo test` — tests rebuild the rlib, not the shared library). The JVM no longer embeds it; `GoldenConformanceTest` guards the Java port against golden-fixture drift. - **Debug comments** (`HtmlRenderer::with_debug_comments(true)`; C ABI `pathland_html_render_debug` / `_fragment_debug`): every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied (`<!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill, width=FILL -->`) — values decoded by protocol type (FILL/HUG sentinels, well-known enums, colors, strings, bitmasks); opt-in so default output is unchanged, and comments stay valid HTML (content scrubbed of `--`). ## Cross-renderer conformance (no drift) The **`pathland-html-golden`** crate renders a battery of scenarios to committed fixtures under `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html` canonical `render_fragment`). Its `tests/guard.rs` fails if the SSR output changes without the fixtures being regenerated (`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`), and the TypeScript `test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` asserts the DOM client reproduces the same DOM from the same batches (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta). The SSR output is the contract both renderers must satisfy. ## Not implemented / gaps - **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** (spec/LAYOUT.md §content fitting): aligned — it **alone** has no observable effect (the old `nowrap`+`text-overflow:ellipsis` emission is gone, SSR + TS DOM client); under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp the renderer tail- ellipsizes via `line-clamp`. Renderer-owned fidelity: CSS cannot place a head/middle ellipsis, so non-Tail modes fall back to the tail ellipsis. - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset (colors, font size/weight/family, spacing/padding/content margins, corner radius, opacity, width/height, border width/color, shadow color/x/y/radius). **Parent-path fallback and per-component native control chrome are not implemented in CSS** (see the gaps above). - **Grid/ScrollView/Lazy layout (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView)**: grids emit `gap` from `SPACING`, equal-`1fr` track templates from the `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` constructor properties (columns for GRID/ LAZY_VGRID, rows for LAZY_HGRID + `grid-auto-flow:column`), **`GRID_TRACKS`** per-track specs (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>` → `1fr`/`<pts>px`/ `minmax(<pts>px,1fr)`, taking precedence over the count), and **per-cell alignment** — each cell is wrapped in an auto-placed shell whose `justify-self`/`align-self` is `stretch` for a `FILL`/greedy cell, else the grid `ALIGNMENT` position (default start) — with `justify-items`/ `align-items` on the container. **`GRID_ROW`** (0x1D) rows are flattened with explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` placement; each row renders as a transparent `<div style="display:contents">` (its id hydrates the DOM client), and a short row leaves trailing columns empty. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` on a grid are the universal pixel box, never a count. `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;overflow:auto`) and renders **only its first child** (the spec-pinned single content). Conformance cases C11–C14 covered by the SSR tests + golden fixtures (incl. the `gridrow` scenario). - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property). - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact. - **Parent-path token fallback is not implemented in CSS**: overriding a parent path (e.g. `font.body`) does not derive leaf variables (`font.body.size`). Override the leaf paths on the web. - **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — no external/webfont loading, so the rendered document makes no network requests for fonts and works offline. An app can still pick its own typeface via a `font.body.family` `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override (any STRING value, e.g. `"Inter"` if the app hosts it). - Compound token refs cover shadow x/y/radius and border width (the DOM client mirrors them); per-component tokens still style only the component CSS the renderer owns. ## Verified by `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 77 headless render tests (components, properties, composite, event attrs, navigation slot route/transition attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames, inline-all styling, built-in CSS block contents, Inter CDN head links, design tokens: base/dark override CSS, `px` lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, generative `space.N`). The built-in CSS tests assert the generated bundle is embedded (reset, tokens, component rules) and that component rules reference the catalog/metadata tokens; the linked-mode tests assert the hashed `<link>` and that the default render remains inline. `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` — the SSR golden-fixture guard. `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check` and `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` validate the design pipeline and the committed bundle.

state.output: # pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native library). Protocol contract: `spec/`. ## Implemented - **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` / `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes. - **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario. - **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta`/`render(frame, root, meta)` / `renderLinked(..., meta)` add canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter cards, and component-derived JSON-LD (WebPage + Article for `ROLE_ARTICLE`). Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` win; the metadata values are fallbacks. The document output is pinned byte-for-byte against the Rust renderer's `document_meta.document.html` fixture. - **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and size-that-fits snapshots. - **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` / `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed ``; `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving. - **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers. - **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `identity (the `uiId` map key) is deliberately separate from the persisted-state scope (the client's `wid`, carried only on the WebSocket URL — never in the page URL, so the address bar stays clean). The SSR request therefore has no `wid`: `renderHtml(route, wid)` with a null `wid` renders defaults; the client's live session is scoped by the WS `wid`, and a same-tab reload re-syncs that window's persisted state over the WebSocket. The old `session` cookie is removed. - **`PathlandSession`** — per-session: builds the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal, mounts `app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath)))`, **delta-batched send-on-`endFrame`** (`DeltaBatcher` coalesces per-signal frames into one batch — flush ~20 ms or 16 KB, string offsets rebased — so a continuous input burst can't overflow a remote WebSocket send queue), `applyEnvironment` (re-route guard-aware via the bound router), `dispatch` (tap/nav-intent/text/value/date/NAVIGATE), `resync`, `renderHtml`, `close`. Runtime theming: `setTheme(ThemeData)`, `resetTheme()`, and `setColorScheme(ThemeMode)` emit one `META::RESET_THEME` + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` frame or `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` to the live client (renderer state; no tree re-emission). The SSR document keeps the mount theme until a resync/reload. `sendBatch` drops the connection on any send failure (a client reconnect then re-syncs via `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket); `closeConnection` best-effort closes an `AutoCloseable` adapter (the starters now close their underlying WebSocket on failure). Now takes the app's `base` and `stateScope` explicitly (the registry supplies them). - **`DeltaBatcher`** — merges session delta frames (opcodes + a single rebased string section) and flushes as one network batch on a timer/byte threshold; the Java analogue of the Rust transport's `Batcher`. It owns the per-session **message sequence** (stamped on each flushed batch via `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)`) so the DOM client can detect a lost batch and recover with `META::RESYNC` (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection); an empty flush consumes no sequence. The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. Coalescing tests cover merging + rebasing, a 100-frame burst collapsing to one send, incrementing sequences, and a blocking sender not holding the lock. - **`PathlandConnection`** — the transport seam (`send(byte[])`/`isOpen()`); each starter adapts its WebSocket type to it. - **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits session open/close, inbound event batches, inbound drops (oversize/rate), flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes + merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/ `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays nothing). This module also ships the `dev.pathland.observability` Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62. - **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler` cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count (no lost effects, no cross-session values). - **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}` (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in this module in main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal jar; the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it. - **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied fallback. The `dev.pathland.state.redis.RedisStateStore` (Lettuce) ships in this module too. - **Observability adapters** — `dev.pathland.observability.MicrometerTelemetry` turns the seam into `pathland.*` meters (counters, timers, a distribution summary, a pull-based sessions gauge, every meter tagged by `mount`); the optional `TracingTelemetry` decorator emits an OpenTelemetry span per frame send / inbound event batch / SSR render. Micrometer is a compile dependency; the OTel API is `optional`, so a host that does not enable tracing pays nothing. - **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`). - **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base. - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml` emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `` when set, and the DOM client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script. `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it). ## Not implemented / gaps - No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory). - Quarkus mounted-app WebSocket endpoints require a **single-segment** mount path (the `/{app}` path param); Spring supports any depth. ## Proxy views (spec/PROXY.md) — M1 (live) - **`proxy.ProxyIdMap`** — node-id namespacing: the reserved high range `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)`, 1024 blocks of `2^20`, the block math, and the opcode remap in both directions (`TREE` node ids + the node-id-bearing `PARAMETER` ops `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` on ingress; `EVENT` targets on egress; `META` untouched). `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **not** remapped — its `A` is a token-path arena offset, not a node id (remapping it produced a huge out-of-bounds string offset → the client's RESYNC loop; regression-tested). maps, `applyEnvironment`/`resync`/`close` idempotent, registry SSR + lifecycle/teardown, **two windows with the same `wid` still get separate sessions** (a tap to one never reaches the other), and respect, no-root-mount 404, per-app base + state scope, duplicate-mount rejection, normalization, SSR emits the mounted app's base. `PathlandTelemetryTest`: a recording telemetry double asserts the registry emits session/event/resync/flush/SSR/close events, the host binds the active-sessions gauge, a failed send reports `connectionFailed`, and `DeltaBatcher` reports the flushed batch. `proxy.ProxySessionTest` (a fake origin transport): the ENVIRONMENT+RESYNC handshake + handshake headers, snapshot retry when the first RESYNC is lost, snapshot remap + root attachment, delta remap with the string section passed through verbatim, event egress unmapped, pointer-move coalescing, `META::RESET` → scoped teardown, disconnect teardown, and the chatty-origin drop+resync breaker. `proxy.ProxyIntegrationTest`: a `ProxyView` in the app tree opens an origin connection on `connect`, the remapped origin snapshot reaches the client (with the root attached), a client event in the proxy range routes back to the origin unmapped, and the SSR document embeds the origin subtree (remapped ids) in one render. `FrameMergerTest`: splicing a proxy's origin frame into an SSR frame rebases its string offsets (SET_TEXT / LIST / STRING operands) and returns the base unchanged when there is nothing to append.--- # pathland-quarkus — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin` capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`. ## Implemented - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`: `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes), `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout, reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`. `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance. - **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly, Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults; application config (including `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins. - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount. - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt. - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: `IndexResource` derives the canonical URL from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry; `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`. - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session). - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps: the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment. Same stateless rule as the root socket. - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead) dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped); SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS); per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS. **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`** serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`. - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`) to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`. - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see. - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) + `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear at `/q/metrics`. - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`. Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued), and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection / a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it). - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG` **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat. - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`) no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed). - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension. - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. parts.text:
Need more on modifiers for text style, foreground, background, role, accessibility. Also inspect Components constants (is there ICON? yes 0x09 likely). And HTML renderer semantic roles for list items: bullets? Let's inspect design CSS components and reset. Also table support? No table component. Grid can lay out table. But semantic <table>? Not available via role. Need check role spec. Also whether external link opening works; LinkRun href rendered `<a>`. Is there target=_blank? Probably not.

Also docs site needs:
- Markdown block parser -> Kotlin DSL views. Could add a `Markdown` view builder in Kotlin that parses block markdown (JVM) into DSL views. Could use a Java markdown library (commonmark-java) or implement. But protocol constraints? No need; it's app-side. However rendering from a component's `body()` or a `View` that builds child nodes. Need block AST. We can add to pathland-view-core or a separate library to avoid bloating core. The user says "it must be via Kotlin DSL" - likely means docs content should be defined with the Kotlin DSL, not necessarily raw markdown only? They say "For the documentation sites I would prefer to be able to describe it using markdown. Not markdown via text views, as we need support for more markdown (images, table etc.)." Then "It must be via the kotlin dsl." So they want a Kotlin DSL API like `Markdown("""...""")` that produces rich views. Could also be a `MarkdownPage` component. Need to design.

Let me inspect what text styles exist, role mapping, HTML renderer CSS for list/table, and whether code spans are styled. Also investigate ability to embed raw CSS? The renderer owns CSS, design tokens. For a marketing site, probably enough. But documentation code blocks with syntax highlighting require multiple color spans in one text; attributed text supports colors. So possible: highlight code into AttributedString with color runs and monospace. Need a highlighter.

Tables: build using Grid. Semantics: HTML `<table>` not possible; but can approximate with grid + role table/grid? Role spec includes GRID? Let me check Roles; only LIST/LIST_ITEM etc. No TABLE roles. Protocol roles catalog limited. Could add TABLE/ROW/CELL roles or use GRID component. For accessibility and docs, semantic table would be nice. Need a plan.

Markdown block parser: commonmark-java is a dependency possibility on JVM. But Pathland prefers no external deps? pathland-view-core is pure Java/Kotlin with JNA. Adding commonmark-java is fine, but maybe they want their own parser. Also `pathland-markdown` shared crate is inline only. Since requirement is Kotlin DSL, implement a JVM block parser in pathland-view-core (or a new `pathland-markdown` JVM module?) Reuse inline Markdown parser for inline content.

Need look at how `View` and components build. Could implement `MarkdownContent` as a `View` that parses markdown and emits a VStack of blocks. Need signal/state? static content. For dynamic maybe not.

Also docs site functionality: sidebar, header nav, search. Search: could be client-side JS using index embedded? Or server search endpoint. But Pathland is declarative; a search field + results list can be built. Need content index. For a static-ish docs site, server can load `.md` files. But user says it must be via Kotlin DSL—maybe they don't want a content directory loaded at runtime; they want markdown embedded in Kotlin? Could be both: DSL function `Markdown(md: String)` with content as Kotlin raw strings. But for docs, a content pipeline might be desired. The phrase "It must be via the kotlin dsl" clarifies that the implementation/authoring should be Kotlin DSL, not Rust or a separate renderer. So I should propose Kotlin DSL APIs: `Markdown` view, `MarkdownPage`, table/list components, docs layout, etc.

Let me inspect:
- Constants components, roles, text styles, properties (code).
- HTML renderer role_spec and css for `ul/li`, `table`, headings.
- Kotlin View modifier API for `role`, `textStyle`, `fontDesign`, `foregroundStyle`, `background`, `size`, `link`? Let's grep.

parts.text:
Now let's inspect the HTML renderer's CSS output for lists and headings to assess default typography. In inline CSS, TEXT_STYLE likely maps to sizes/weights. But list bullets are removed by reset and no `.pathland` rule for ul. So lists need renderer CSS for role LIST/LIST_ITEM (bullets) or app-level bullets. Since renderer-owned, adding `ul` list styling in design CSS would be needed or custom bullet views.

Need inspect design/tokens typography and component CSS maybe there's docs styles? `design/html/components.css` only controls. Let's see rest. Not crucial.

Need understand Kotlin DSL's ability to build docs layout. There is no `Markdown` block view. Need add.

Let's inspect the PathlandPhantom: `pathland-view-core` maybe has `components/Markdown`? grep "Markdown" only inline. Let's check.

Also check JS DOM renderer capabilities: hydration, etc. Fine.

Now, hosting: Quarkus SSR route and assets. Could build with Quarkus; docs markdown files in resources. Need a content loader. But user says must be via Kotlin DSL. Could still load markdown strings into Kotlin view. Perhaps "it must be via Kotlin DSL" means they want the site built using the Kotlin DSL (not the Rust DSL), and documentation pages authored in markdown rendered by a Kotlin DSL `Markdown` component. I should confirm.

Let's explore design tokens for typography, code colors, and whether there's a "docs" style. Also check README screenshot and the existing demo. Then formulate gaps.

Potential gaps:

1. Block-level Markdown parser + renderer (biggest). Currently only inline. Need:
   - CommonMark/GFM-ish block parsing: headings, paragraphs, lists (ordered/unordered/nested/task), code fences, blockquotes, thematic breaks, tables (GFM), images, links, HTML? (should not allow raw HTML), footnotes maybe.
   - Inline additions: images, autolinks, escaped characters, hard line breaks; maybe inline code already.
   - A Kotlin DSL `Markdown(text)` or `MarkdownPage(frontmatter)` view that maps blocks to DSL components.
   - Heading IDs/anchors/TOC + slugger.
   - Reference-style links and link resolution (internal routes vs external href).
   - External links: current links are `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` link runs -> `<a href>`; does DOM client handle clicks? Need see if links are intercepted/navigation. The SSR emits `<a href>`; browser handles navigation. If docs is SPA-ish, internal links would full page load or router? Could accept full page load (SSR), but better intercept internal links => router navigation. Need add link handling (relative markdown link -> navigation intent).
   - Images: IMAGE with LABEL alt, content mode, width. Markdown image syntax parse into standalone Image block; inline images? Markdown images can be inline. AttributedString has no image run. Could support only block images or new inline image capability. Need decide.
   - Tables: Need a table component or DSL composition. Existing GRID can create grid but it's not semantic table; support cell borders/header background/column widths/alignment. Better add a `Table` DSL builder composing Grid/VStack; possibly protocol ROLE_TABLE/ROW/CELL or renderer-native `<table>` via a new component. Since requirement is Kotlin DSL, could implement a `Table` view using existing components with HSTACK/VSTACK and borders. But accessible semantics and responsive behavior need roles. Alternatively add semantic roles TABLE/ROW/COLUMN_HEADER/CELL to protocol (renderer-owned) and compose. That's a protocol change, requires spec/constants/both renderers/tests. Given user asks what we lack, this is a key gap. Could also use `Grid` + `accessibilityRole` but roles don't include table. `ROLE` catalog would need new roles.
   - Styled code blocks: syntax highlighting. AttributedString supports color and weight, so build a highlighter producing runs; monospace via FONT_DESIGN; background via view. But line-by-line spans? If one text node with newlines, HTML `<span>` with `white-space`? Text rendering currently likely no `white-space: pre-wrap`? Need check. Code blocks need preserved whitespace and horizontal scroll. Could render each line as monospace Text with no trimming? But HTML collapses spaces unless CSS `white-space: pre`. The renderer may not emit white-space. There's no `WHITE_SPACE` property. So code blocks need a property or component. This is a real gap. Let's check renderer for `white-space`.

parts.text:
The grep output got polluted by node_modules. Need focused search excluding design/node_modules. Let me use grep tool with path. But I have enough.

Key gaps identified:
- No block markdown.
- No semantic table roles / table component. GRID can lay out but no table semantics/anchor.
- No code-block whitespace preservation (`white-space: pre`) or syntax highlighting; attributed text supports styling, so highlighting possible, but renderer needs `white-space`. Check if TEXT has a property for whitespace. No. Could compose code lines using Text with monospace and each line separate, but spaces collapse. Need `white-space: pre` support in renderer. Could use `LINE_LIMIT`? no. Need new property or component, or renderer maps FONT_DESIGN MONOSPACED to pre-wrap? That'd be weird. Alternatively use non-breaking spaces on line-leading whitespace; hacky. Better add `WHITE_SPACE` property or `CODE`/`CODE_BLOCK` primitive/role. But user wants Kotlin DSL, could still require renderer support.
- No list bullet/numbered rendering. Role LIST→ul, LIST_ITEM→li, but reset removes list style; no CSS for list items. So either add renderer CSS to restore list-style, or app builds bullets as text/HStack. For docs, use HStack with bullet Text and content. But accessible semantic lists would need CSS. Also ordered lists need counters, no protocol property for numbering. Could render numbers as Text. Nested lists indentation handled by nesting VStacks.
- No blockquote styling (can compose with border-left manually).
- No heading anchor IDs/TOC. Heading TEXT_STYLE maps to h1-h5 but there's no `anchor` id property or link. Need slug IDs. Could add a `VIEW_ID`/`ANCHOR` property? There is no HTML id property. DOM node IDs are `data-pathland-id`, not HTML id. Documentation anchors need element IDs (e.g., `#getting-started`). Need protocol property or renderer derives from heading text (slug). Could add `ANCHOR` string property and render `id`. Also heading links/copy anchor icons, TOC generation from parsed AST.
- No h6 (heading styles only up to h5); minor.
- No frontmatter/page metadata pipeline. Could use Kotlin data class.
- No docs navigation/layout components (sidebar, TOC, breadcrumbs, prev/next). Can build with DSL, but need Sticky? ScrollView, VStack. Maybe no sticky property? CSS position sticky not available. Could use fixed layout with independent ScrollViews. `ScrollView` works, but header/sidebar fixed? Use HStack with sidebar and content; fine. For a top nav, use HStack. No `position: sticky`; can use frame + scroll independently.
- No link click interception for internal docs links. AttributedText links render `<a href>`; browser full navigation => SSR works (server renders route) so acceptable. But if using Router, full reload is okay. To have SPA transitions, intercept links; not essential.
- No search. Can implement in Kotlin with a search field and precomputed index, but dynamic filtering based on text input requires signals; available. Client-side JS? Could also add server endpoint. But static content index in Kotlin is fine. Need a search UI and index. This is app-level, not core.
- No syntax highlighting library in JVM; app-level.
- No image handling for local docs images: assets served from `/_pathland/assets` or demo asset route. Need a static asset convention for docs (e.g., `/assets/docs/...`). There is `DemoAssetsRoute`; inspect. Also images in markdown need dimensions/alt and maybe captions.
- No image block responsive width; IMAGE has CONTENT_MODE/ASPECT_RATIO. Fine.
- No block-level markdown images inline vs block; need parse.
- No tables with alignment, header, colspan/rowspan; GFM tables only simple.
- No syntax highlighting and copy-code buttons. A copy button needs JS or platform clipboard; could use Button with an action that writes clipboard via app? Not in protocol. Could omit or implement JS. Not core.
- No docs site versioning (app-level).
- No "raw HTML" in markdown (should reject).
- No inline code background styling? Attributed text code runs get monospace but no background/padding. Could only do whole view. Fine.
- No `Link` with internal route nav intent. Could add DSL `MarkdownLink` mapping. App-level.

Also for marketing site, likely lacks:
- Hero/landing layout is possible with stacks/zstack/images/colors.
- No CSS animations/transitions except hover? Protocol explicitly excludes hover styles; renderer handles interaction states. Marketing sites may want scroll effects; not critical.
- No `position: sticky`, `max-width` container? `frame(maxWidth)` exists. Fine.
- No custom fonts/webfont? Design token string can set `font.body.family`, but no font loading. Could host font CSS externally? design says no external font requests by default; app can override family but browser needs font available. Could add `@font-face` via CSS? Renderer-owned CSS only. Maybe not needed.
- No SVG logo? ICON is fixed Remix icons; SHAPE Path placeholder, no custom SVG asset. Could use IMAGE with SVG/PNG for logo. Fine.
- No external asset hosting/dimensions maybe.
- No `video` autoplay? VIDEO controller.
- No scroll animations; not needed.

Need inspect `IMAGE` properties: width, aspect ratio, content mode, label. Fine.

Need inspect docs site hosting: Quarkus demo asset route can serve files. Let's look.
